text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

VEGOIL SALE - Egypt's official Holding Company for Food Industries said it bought a total 69,000 tonnes of palm, sunflower and degummed soy oils at prices between $546.50 and $565 per tonne for delivery in April and May.

CORN SALE - The Philippines' National Food Authority (NFA) on Wednesday bought 25,000 tonnes of U.S. white corn at $201.80 per tonne, an NFA official said. The corn will be bought through Continental Grain Co which won the bidding, NFA Administrator Eduardo Gomez said.
CORN AND OILSEED SALE - South Korea bought at least 1,326,150 tonnes of grain and oilseeds in March through tenders and private negotiations, traders said.

CORN AND WHEAT TENDER - The Cyprus Grain Commission on Wednesday invited tenders for the supply of an combined shipment of 10,000 tonnes spring and 8,000 tonnes durum wheat, and a shipment of 18,000 tonnes of corn. Shipment for the combined wheat cargo is scheduled at the end of April or the beginning of May, while the corn shipment is scheduled for the beginning of May. Both tenders close on April 8.
WHEAT TENDER - Four Manila flour millers rejected for the second time on Wednesday offers for the supply of 70,000 tonnes of Canadian and U.S. wheat.
- A Turkish trading company and flour producer said the company was buying 20,000 tonnes of milling wheat from Argentina to produce flour for export purposes.

CORN TENDER - South Korea on Tuesday invited tenders to buy 52,500 tonnes of U.S. yellow No.2 corn. Traders said shipment was set for July 1-20 if sourced from the U.S. Gulf, July 15-August 5 if sourced from the Pacific Northwest, or June 20-July 10 if from Argentina. Arrival was set for Inchon.

LENTIL TENDER - Syria's General Establishment for Cereal Processing and Trade has offered 16,000 tonnes of lentils for export, an official spokesman said. An international call for prices setting April 8 as final date to receive bids had been issued. Confirmation would be made on April 9. The spokesman said the lentils of the 1996 crop would be ready for shipment in May. Partial offers will be acceptable up to 1,000 tonnes and the establishment has the right for partial confirmation.
BARLEY TENDER - The South African Wheat Board said it was offering 25,150 tonnes of feed grade barley for export sale no later than April 30.
RICE TENDERS - Iran is seeking to buy 400,000 tonnes of rice from Thailand but a deal has not been concluded yet, Thai Commerce Minister Narongchai Akrasanee said on Monday.
- Syria seeks 12,000 tonnes of white rice for shipment between April 20 and May 20. April 8 is the final date for bids and result will be announced on April 16.

MARKET TALK - China could be in the market for wheat later this year but no sales were being planned at present, the Australian Wheat Board said. Chinese demand for imported wheat was down because of its strong current crop. But later, if China showed itself to be an active buyer on international markets, the AWB said it expected it would be one of the main parties negotiating sales.... Sri Lanka's rice imports in 1997 are seen at 450,000 tonnes largely due to a shift in consumption patterns, a top finance ministry official said. ... Sri Lanka's wheat imports in 1997 are seen at about 750,000 tonnes, lower than last year's imports of nearly a million tonnes, a top finance ministry official said.... Bangladesh's wheat consumption is expected to rise to 3.6 million tonnes in fiscal 1997/98 beginning July from the current year's 2.9 million, the official BSS news agency said....Taiwan's hog crisis has begun hitting the island's edible oil producers, who said on Wednesday a fall in demand for soy-based feed was forcing them to cut production and turn to oil imports.
